summary: Held through several normal dips (each recovering, reversion_prob staying 0.85-0.99 and lambda staying positive) while the trade ran as high as +13.25pts. Bailed at frame 26 when price suddenly broke to -13.5pts -- a new worst level by far, more than 7x any prior drawdown -- and critically the 5s reversion_prob collapsed to 0.141 (versus 0.85-0.99 on every earlier dip) with KMDR confirming continuation rather than reversal. That combination (unprecedented adverse magnitude + collapsed reversion probability + confirming momentum detector) was the wrong-direction signature, distinct from the shallow high-reversion-prob dips that preceded it. Next time I'd watch reversion_prob_30 on the fast timeframe as the primary discriminator between a normal dip and a real breakdown, rather than raw point count alone.
